headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are also plausible via shared MCP/browser surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and browser-based I/O, so a shared channel can carry attacker-controlled content from one into the other. gpt-researcher reads files and web content; TREK uses MCP and real-time collaboration, making instruction-hijack plausible even without a documented direct bridge. Uncertainty remains, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through MCP or copied documents, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF TREK renders or forwards gpt-researcher output without sanitization, attacker instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable MCP between the agents unless provenance tagging is added.
Strip instructions from imported documents before TREK consumes them.
Use a read-only handoff format for gpt-researcher outputs.
Add a human review step before any agent follows external text.
requires-engineering: implement content provenance and instruction filtering.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and secrets, while TREK handles reservations, API keys, MFA secrets, and logs. Both have file and network surfaces, so if they share a workspace or exchange outputs, sensitive travel and research data can leak to external APIs. The blast radius includes secrets and personal records, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the agents share files, then local documents or reservations can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent forwards its context to third-party APIs, secrets in the shared context can leak externally.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared files before handoff.
Restrict outbound network access for one agent during transfers.
Use redacted exports instead of raw documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can run browsers and use networked tools, and gpt-researcher can spawn subprocesses and install packages while TREK is collaborative and uses MCP. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces where concurrent writes or tool actions can interfere, though no direct shared lock is documented. Medium fits because the conflict pathway exists but is not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or database, concurrent writes can collide.
IF TREK and gpt-researcher share browser sessions or MCP resources, tool actions can race.
mitigations: Assign separate directories and databases.
Serialize browser and MCP access with a simple operator schedule.
Avoid running package installs while TREK is active.
Use one agent at a time for mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher pipeline, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK consumes gpt-researcher outputs as authoritative travel facts, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or user-facing plans. Because the downstream impact can affect real actions, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK uses gpt-researcher output as a source of truth, misinformation can propagate.
IF either agent auto-generates plans or reservations from the other's text, downstream mistakes become operational.
mitigations: Require verification before TREK accepts research claims.
Mark gpt-researcher output as untrusted until reviewed.
Limit automatic actions to drafts only.
Add citations and source links to every transferred fact.
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle sensitive personal and account data, but the profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is retention and logging: TREK stores logs and databases, while gpt-researcher handles local documents and secrets. Because the mismatch is plausible but not explicit, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF either agent stores EU personal data in a region without a DPA, residency risk increases.
IF TREK logs secrets or gpt-researcher retains documents longer than intended, retention policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Review retention settings for logs and uploads.
Delete secrets from logs and exports.
Confirm data-region settings for any hosted services.
Limit sensitive fields in shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency and retention controls.
